dossier.official_website: https://vacanzadevelopers.com (taken from the Instagram bio; the site is client-rendered, so I could only see the title and the tagline, not its pages)
dossier.what_they_do: Local Surat real-estate developer. Residential (2 BHK flats at Vacanza City, 150 Feet VIP Road, Althan-Bamroli), commercial (Vacanza Shopping Street, 1000-15,000 sq ft spaces), and premium offices and showrooms (Vacanza Atlas, Vesu Canal Road). https://www.instagram.com/vacanzadevelopers/ via WebFetch: public bio of a developer for homes, shops and offices, 3,345 followers, website listed as vacanzadevelopers.com. This is the only place I found the official site address.

https://www.commonfloor.com/vacanza-developers/builder/9aswqf via WebFetch: builder listing with an office address at Vacanza Harrod's, 200 Ft Road, Udhana-Magdalla, Vesu, Surat 395007. It shows 1 ongoing project (unnamed), 0 completed, and no founder names, year established, builder phone or email. This is a second independent source that the business exists.

Meta Ad Library data via the Apify actor apify/facebook-ads-scraper, run on the Facebook page URL, active ads only, limit 6 (about US$0.03). Returned 6 active ads from Page 'Vacanza Developers' (4,101 likes) with CTA, body text, start dates and platforms. This is the re-check of the finder's claim.

https://www.facebook.com/ads/library/?id=1594782351731890 (the finder's evidence URL): WebFetch returned 403 and the Apify web-fetch timed out after 120 s. I could not open this exact ad. I re-checked the Page's ads through the scraper instead, and that ad ID was not among the 6 returned.

https://vacanzadevelopers.com/ via Apify web-fetch and rag-web-browser: HTTP 200, title 'Vacanza Developers', description 'Home - Vacanza Developers Ghar Hai To Jahaan Ha...', but the body is only a Next.js loader gif. No contact page, owner name or RERA data could be read. WebFetch and www.vacanzadevelopers.com returned 403, and vacanzadevelopers.in failed.
https://www.facebook.com/vacanzadevelopers/about via Apify web-fetch: HTTP 413 (response over the size limit), nothing read.

magicbricks.com (blocked by the fetch tool) and 99acres.com (403): both were guessed URLs and returned nothing. The WebSearch budget was exhausted, so no Google Maps, RERA or press check was possible.

contacts.note: Printed by the business in the body of its Vacanza Atlas ad (start date 2026-10-16) as the enquiry and site-visit number. The finder reported the same number in ad 1594782351731890, which I could not open. Indian mobile, so likely WhatsApp-capable (not confirmed). Unknown whether it is the owner's line, a sales desk or an agency's.
Official site per the Instagram bio. Not readable by my tools (client-rendered). Contact and enquiry pages unchecked, so an email or form may exist there.
Business Page, 4,101 followers. Do not message it as a prospect.
Business account, 3,345 followers, links to the site.
Third-party builder listing with the Vesu office address only. It has no builder phone or email, and the contactus@commonfloor.com address belongs to the portal, not the builder.

observed_facts.fact: Page 'Vacanza Developers' had 6 active Meta ads in my sample (limit 6, so the real count may be higher). Start dates run from 2026-10-16 to 2026-10-23. The ad IDs are 2433420887396586, 2888274911535780, 2671300023268401, 1766533534650500, 2103795657243686 and 1683522276522217.

5 of the 6 ads have CTA WHATSAPP_MESSAGE ('Send WhatsApp message'). The sixth has CTA 'Book now' with link api.whatsapp.com/send. All 6 list WhatsApp among the publisher platforms, alongside Facebook, Instagram and, for one ad, Audience Network.

The ads cover three product lines: a 2 BHK booking offer at Vacanza City (Rs 4 lakh to book, 'No EMI till possession', 150 Feet VIP Road, Althan-Bamroli), commercial and clinic spaces at Vacanza Shopping Street, and offices and showrooms at Vacanza Atlas (510-1700 sq ft, Vesu Canal Road). Formats are video, image and dynamic-creative.

The ad copy closes with a call or enquiry ask: 'Aaj hi call karein aur site visit/bookings ki details jaaniye', 'Aaj hi enquiry karein', 'Enquire Now for Details & Site Visit' with +91 90999 73209. The 2 BHK ad (started 2026-10-21) says '5 Days Left', so that offer ended around 2026-10-26.
Facebook Page: 4,101 followers, 1,397 talking about this, 134 were here, category Construction Company, Surat.
Instagram @vacanzadevelopers has 3,345 followers and lists the website vacanzadevelopers.com.
CommonFloor lists the builder with an office at Vacanza Harrod's, Vesu, Surat 395007 (1 ongoing project). The page names no founders and gives no year established.

Three of the 6 ads show an end date of 2026-10-24 or 2026-10-25 while still flagged active. Meta typically shows the last delivery date for active ads, but it is unresolved whether these are still running on 2026-10-26.

hypotheses: INFERENCE: Click-to-WhatsApp enquiries from several simultaneous ads probably arrive in the evening and at night. A time-boxed offer ('5 Days Left') makes reply speed matter more. Nothing observed shows how fast they actually reply.

INFERENCE: The ad copy pushes 'call' and 'site visit' and prints a phone number next to a WhatsApp button, so first replies are probably handled by people. This is not observed, and an auto-greeting or a WhatsApp Business API system may already exist.
INFERENCE: With four product lines, WhatsApp enquiries probably land with no shared list for the sales team. The evidence is only that the ads run several lines under one Page.

INFERENCE: The mix of dynamic-creative ads, several lines and a dated promotion suggests an in-house marketer or an ad agency runs the campaigns. An agency could hold the WhatsApp setup and be the real gatekeeper.

INFERENCE: The ad burst coincides with the festival season (Diwali is about 8 Nov 2026) and may be a seasonal push, not a year-round stream. The finder's 'continuous' is not shown by my data, which covers only about 10 days.
dossier.ability_to_pay: A multi-project developer in Surat with residential, retail and premium office stock in Vesu and Althan. At least 6 verified active ads in the same week across several formats and platforms, plus a 4,101-follower Page and an Instagram account. Spend is not disclosed, and I saw no ad history before 2026-10-16. The pay signal is relative to a small automation subscription, not a measured budget.
dossier.decision_maker: not found. No public page I could read names an owner, director or sales head (CommonFloor and the Facebook and Instagram pages name nobody). The official site could not be rendered, so a team or about page may exist there.
dossier.size_cues: Four named product lines or projects (Vacanza City, Atlas, Shopping Street, Homes; the last is from the finder, not re-verified). Offices in Vesu (Harrod's). CommonFloor shows only 1 ongoing project and no years in business. Facebook: 4,101 followers and 134 check-ins. Instagram: 3,345 followers. This is a mid-size local developer with no sign of being a chain or franchise. The finder's 'Page created 2017' is unverified.
dossier.resistance: Unknown, not high on the evidence. I found no sign of a bot, a WhatsApp BSP or a CRM, and no anti-AI positioning, but I could not see the site. Likely gatekeepers are an ad agency or a marketing person behind the ads. The owner is not named, so the first conversation would be with whoever answers the printed sales line. The ad copy leans on calls and site visits, which suggests a human-led sales culture. Past Campaign 1 results (cold WhatsApp templates 0/3) argue against a cold WhatsApp opener.
dossier.case_for: Real, verified local developer (Facebook Page, Instagram and CommonFloor all agree). It actively buys Meta ads, and at least 6 were live in the same week, mostly with a WhatsApp button that sends enquiries to WhatsApp. The ad copy pushes site visits and booking enquiries, and a dated offer makes reply speed matter. Nothing in the data points to a duplicate, a chain or a competitor, and a sales number is published in its own ad.
dossier.case_against: The need is only inferred: a WhatsApp CTA is standard for Indian real-estate ads and does not show slow replies. I could not open the finder's ad, check the site, find an owner or email, or confirm the number is a sales desk and not an agency's. The ad stream may be a festival-season burst, and an agency or an existing auto-reply may already cover the need. This sits at the weak edge of B and drops to C if the number turns out to be an agency line or the site shows a working chatbot or WhatsApp Business API setup.
dossier.best_angle: Ask, do not assert. Open with their live Vacanza City 2 BHK and Atlas ads ('Send WhatsApp message' button, Rs 4 lakh booking offer): 'Someone taps your button at 11 pm. Does anyone reply before morning?' Then offer a first reply in about a minute with the brochure, 3 quick questions and a site-visit slot, and one list for the sales team across all four projects. Do not claim they reply slowly.
dossier.best_channel: A human phone call to the sales number printed in their own ad (+91 90999 73209), asking for the owner or sales head and for an email address. It is the only business-published route found. Do not use a cold WhatsApp template (0/3 in Campaign 1), and do not message through the ad button or the Page, since that would pose as a buyer. Before calling, someone should open vacanzadevelopers.com in a normal browser to find an email, form or owner name and to check for an existing chatbot.
gaps: The finder's evidence ad (id 1594782351731890) was not opened. The scraper returned only 6 ads, so '10 ads at once' is unverified and 6 is the confirmed count.
The official site is JavaScript-rendered and unreadable by my tools: no owner name, no email, no contact form, no check for a chatbot or WhatsApp widget.
No Google Maps, Gujarat RERA, press or justdial check. The WebSearch budget was exhausted and the other directories I tried blocked the fetch.
I cannot tell whether the ad end dates of 2026-10-24 and 2026-10-25 mean the ads stopped, or whether the stream is continuous. Ad spend is not visible.
No evidence on how fast they actually reply, and I did not test it because I may not enquire as a customer.
The WhatsApp number behind the ad button is not exposed in the ad library (the link is api.whatsapp.com/send with no number). I do not know if it is the same as +91 90999 73209.
Total Apify spend came to about US$0.05, at the cap, so no further paid lookups were made.

challenge.business: Vacanza Developers (Surat) - Vacanza City, Atlas, Harrod's, Shopping Street, Homes and others; site vacanzadevelopers.com

checks.claim: Business exists as described and is the right entity (not a namesake)
checks.note: Own site vacanzadevelopers.com (rendered with a 10 s wait on 2026-10-26) lists the same projects as the ads (Atlas, Harrod's, Shopping Street, Homes, City). It links to the same Facebook and Instagram handles. CommonFloor (https://www.commonfloor.com/vacanza-developers/builder/9aswqf) gives a Vesu, Surat office address. Facebook title 'Vacanza Developers | Surat' and Instagram (3,345 followers, site link) agree. At least 3 independent sources, so it passes the 'unverifiable' test.

checks.claim: It is an end developer, not a chain, franchise, agency or vendor
checks.note: Own site says it is a developer using an SPV-per-project model with investors. No sign of a franchise or agency. Not in the duplicate list.

checks.claim: Size: 'mid-size local developer with four product lines'
checks.note: Larger than the dossier says. The site lists 17 project pages, shows 6 running, 7 completed and 3 upcoming, and claims USD 50 million of completed work and 5,000+ customers (https://vacanzadevelopers.com/ and /about). These are self-claims, not independently checked. The self-description is inconsistent: 'within 7 years of inception' on the home page versus 'since 2006' and '15+ years' on /about. The careers page has tabs for a Sales and Business Development team and a Customer Relationship team, so an in-house sales and CRM function probably exists (hypothesis). Still within 'small and mid-size local developer', but at the upper end.

checks.claim: Phone +91 90999 73209 is the business's own number (dossier: unknown whether owner, sales desk or agency)
checks.note: The number is published as a phone and as an api.whatsapp.com/send WhatsApp link on the business's own site, on /contact and in the footer of every page I opened. A second number, (+91) 81416 71000, is published the same way. Both are Indian mobiles, so likely WhatsApp-capable, and the site itself links them to WhatsApp. So the ad number is not an agency's line as far as the site shows.

checks.claim: No business email found
checks.note: info@vacanzadevelopers.com is published on https://vacanzadevelopers.com/contact, with a contact form (Name, Phone, Email, Subject, Message) next to it. The dossier only missed it because its tool did not render the JavaScript.

checks.claim: Decision-maker not found / owner not named
checks.note: https://vacanzadevelopers.com/leadership names two directors. Mohit Agrawal is the director who leads the company. Ankit Agrawal is the director who heads sales and marketing, which is the buyer role for this offer. Both are named by the business itself. I did not look them up on social media.

checks.claim: Official site could not be read (client-rendered)
checks.note: It reads fine when rendered with a wait. Home, /about, /leadership, /contact and /careers all returned HTTP 200 with full text. No chatbot or auto-reply is visible in the page text, but I did not inspect scripts, so a chat widget cannot be ruled out.

checks.claim: Need: 'inferred, not observed' (dossier) versus 'pays for a continuous ad stream ... replies depend on people' (finder)
checks.note: The dossier is right and the finder overstated. Observed: the ads' button opens WhatsApp (investigator's scraper data) and the site's only enquiry routes are plain click-to-chat links, two phone numbers and a contact form. No automated first reply is visible on the site's own pages. Not observed: any slow reply, a missed enquiry, a complaint or the absence of a bot. 'Replies depend on people' is a hypothesis. A WhatsApp button is standard for Indian real-estate ads.

checks.claim: Active ad stream: finder says at least 10 ads live; dossier says 6 confirmed in a limit-6 sample, start dates 2026-10-16 to 2026-10-24
checks.note: I could not reproduce either count. The Ad Library page returned 403 to WebFetch, and the Apify fetch of the finder's ad timed out, so I aborted it to stay under the cap. The investigator's 6-ad sample is plausible and consistent with the site showing several live launches, but '10 at once' and 'continuous' are not shown. The dossier says 3 ads end 24-25 Oct while still flagged active, and the 2 BHK offer was '5 Days Left', so the burst may be seasonal.

checks.claim: Page created 2017 (finder)
checks.note: Not found on any page I could read. It loosely matches the home-page text 'within 7 years of inception' but conflicts with 'since 2006' on /about. Treat as unverified.

checks.claim: Ad detail: 2 BHK at 'Vacanza City, 150 Feet VIP Road, Althan-Bamroli'
checks.note: The site puts 'Vacanza City Residential' at Robot Circle, Pandesara, and the 150 Feet VIP Road / Althan-Bamroli address on Vacanza Bazar and Vacanza Shopping Street. The ad text itself was not re-read by me. Check the location before using it in any copy.

checks.claim: Pay signal is strong
checks.note: Multiple running projects, premium Vesu stock (showrooms, offices, flats), a head office at Vacanza Atlas, a 4,101-follower Facebook Page, a 3,345-follower Instagram account and an active ad burst (6 ads per the investigator). The USD 50M and 5,000-customer figures are self-published only. Ad spend is unknown, but a small automation subscription is clearly affordable.

checks.claim: Existing solution or resistance is unknown and not high
checks.note: No BSP, bot or CRM is named on any page I read, and nothing positions against AI. However, the Customer Relationship team and the Sales and Business Development team shown on the careers page, plus an ad pace that looks agency-run, mean an existing CRM or WhatsApp tool is possible. Not observed either way.

checks.claim: Not a duplicate of an existing lead
checks.note: No name in the 'already in our leads' list matches Vacanza.

checks.claim: Best channel is a phone call to the printed sales number rather than a cold WhatsApp template
checks.note: The call route is still valid. There are now two more business-published routes: the email info@vacanzadevelopers.com and the contact form, addressed to Ankit Agrawal (sales and marketing director). The cold-WhatsApp caution (Campaign 1: 0/3 templates) still stands. Do not message through the ad button or the Facebook Page, because that would pose as a buyer.

challenge.strongest_objection: The need is still only inferred. The only hard evidence is that the ads and the site route enquiries to WhatsApp, which almost every Indian developer does. Nothing shows slow replies or lost buyers. This is also a bigger, more organised company than the dossier assumed: 17 projects, an investor-backed SPV model, an in-house Sales and Business Development team and a Customer Relationship team. It likely already runs a CRM and an ad agency, so a first-reply bot may add little or the agency may be the gatekeeper. The 6-vs-10 ad count and 'continuous' spend could not be reproduced, and the burst may be a Diwali-season push. That is why it is not an A.
corrections: Reach is much better than the dossier says: https://vacanzadevelopers.com/contact publishes info@vacanzadevelopers.com, (+91) 81416 71000 and 90999 73209, both linked to WhatsApp, and a contact form. https://vacanzadevelopers.com/leadership names Mohit Agrawal (Director, leads the company) and Ankit Agrawal (Director, sales and marketing). The dossier's 'no email, no decision-maker' gaps are closed. All of it is business-published.
The ad number 90999 73209 is the business's own published WhatsApp and phone line (site /contact and every page footer), not an unknown or agency line.
The site is readable if rendered with a wait. The dossier's 'unreadable' and 'unchecked' gaps came from the tool, not the site.

Scale is understated. The site shows 17 project pages, 6 running, 7 completed and 3 upcoming, USD 50M completed (self-claim), 5,000+ customers (self-claim) and an SPV-with-investors model. Treat as an upper-mid-size local developer likely with an in-house sales and CRM team (hypothesis).
The site contradicts itself on age ('within 7 years of inception' versus 'since 2006' and '15+ years'). The finder's 'Page created 2017' is unverified.

The '10 ads live' (finder) and 6 ads (investigator) counts are not independently reproducible by me (Ad Library 403, fetch timed out). Use '6 verified by the investigator's scraper on 2026-10-26' and drop 'continuous'.

Need stays INFERRED. Observed facts: a WhatsApp CTA in the ads, a plain click-to-chat link on the site, a contact form and no visible chatbot text. Everything about slow replies or a missing shared list is hypothesis.

Grade stays B and not A, because the need is not observed. It is a strong B on pay and reach. It would move to A only with direct need evidence, for example public reviews or complaints about unanswered calls or WhatsApp, a job post for a manual enquiry or tele-calling role, or a source showing no WhatsApp Business API or auto-reply.

First touch: a human call to the published sales line, or a short email to info@ addressed to Ankit Agrawal, opening with a question about night-time WhatsApp enquiries from their live ads, never a claim that they reply slowly. No cold WhatsApp template and no message through the ad button or Page.
Apify spend for this check was about US$0.04, at the cap, including one aborted Ad Library fetch. WebSearch was out of budget, so no Google Maps, RERA or press check was done.
